$comment: Trusted receiver signer policy, read from the PR base ref only. Evidence must carry a GitHub artifact attestation produced by exactly this pinned, privileged workflow identity, triggered from exactly this source ref (gh attestation verify --signer-workflow --predicate-type --source-ref). check_signer() additionally recomputes the subject digest itself, checks the signer's own certificate sourceRepositoryDigest against approvedSignerSourceDigests, and compares the signed predicate's own definitionSha256/assessedChecks/expectedPredicate fields -- a bare verify exit code is never treated as sufficient. This authenticates that the exact CI assessment recorded by receiver-attest.yml (structural integrity + factory allowlist + capability revocation + independent execution boundary, see assess_canonical) was produced and approved by that pinned workflow AT an approved revision -- not that a local agent's execution or any particular SLSA security level is retroactively certified.
approvedSignerSourceDigestsBootstrap: Deliberately empty (fail-closed): this receiver must never trust a signer revision it has not actually reviewed, and revision trust can never be read from the evidence/predicate itself -- only from the Fulcio/sigstore certificate's own sourceRepositoryDigest field, which the signed content cannot forge. This is a pre-selected-and-reviewed allowlist, never trust-on-first-use: approval must precede that revision ever signing anything, not follow from observing what a first successful run happened to produce. Bootstrap sequence (manual, explicitly authorized, NOT part of this commit; see docs/security-story.md's 'Workflow activation prerequisite'): after activation is authorized, prepare the public evidence in a signing commit S and record approval of that exact revision before publishing it. An explicit push of S to 'refs/heads/examples/enterprise-receiver' supplies an immutable push-event SHA; a later branch update does not rewrite that run's GITHUB_SHA ('gh workflow run --ref <commit SHA>' is NOT a supported substitute -- its documented interface accepts a branch or tag, not a raw SHA). Confirm the signing run's head SHA, certificate sourceRepositoryDigest, and source ref all match the preapproved values -- the observed certificate must never select the value being approved. Only then add the already-approved S to approvedSignerSourceDigests in a separate, subsequent policy commit. Retained attestations from an approved S remain valid after unrelated later commits; a new signing run at any different source SHA needs approval of that new revision, even when the workflow text itself is unchanged.
